conventions.convention: Assume AC. W_p(Σ,m) uses positive integer m and positive-semidefinite scale Σ and is the law of the sum of m independent N_p(0,Σ) outer products. Singular support is allowed; no density is asserted.

Assume AC, n≥2, p≥1 and Σ positive definite. Sampling units are complete iid p-vectors; their scalar coordinates need not be independent. The observation sigma-algebra is the finite product Borel sigma-algebra. Parameters are fixed and inference uses the joint product law.
R is the centered scatter, S=R/(n−1) is the sample covariance, and M=R/n is the separate Gaussian covariance MLE candidate. The definition itself does not establish the MLE property.
Hotelling T² uses n>p and equals n times the sample-mean inverse-S quadratic form on S positive definite, with value zero otherwise. Its stated F law requires the mean null μ=μ₀.

The covariance likelihood ratio is null-over-full, uses the explicit Lebesgue Gaussian density, leaves μ unrestricted under both hypotheses, and uses M=R/n. Its chi-square calibration is asymptotic with p fixed, not finite-sample.
For 0<α<1, reject strictly above the unique (1−α)-quantile of F_{p,n−p}; size is taken over all positive-definite null covariances.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and the sample model with n≥2, p≥1 and Σ positive definite. Then √n(X̄−μ) has law N_p(0,Σ), X̄ is independent of S, and (n−1)S has law W_p(Σ,n−1). If n>p, S is positive definite almost surely.

Assume AC. Let 1≤p≤m and let G be a p×m matrix whose columns are independent N_p(0,I_p) random vectors. Then the first p columns are linearly independent almost surely. Consequently GGᵀ is positive definite almost surely.
Assume AC. Let m≥p≥1, W have law W_p(I_p,m), and Z have law N_p(0,I_p), independently of W. Then W is positive definite almost surely and ((m−p+1)/p)ZᵀW⁻¹Z has law F_{p,m−p+1}.

Assume AC, n>p≥1, and the iid multivariate-normal sample model with Σ positive definite. For specified μ₀, define T²=n(X̄−μ₀)ᵀS⁻¹(X̄−μ₀) when S is positive definite and zero otherwise. Under μ=μ₀, ((n−p)/(p(n−1)))T² has law F_{p,n−p}.

Assume AC, fixed p≥1, n>p and the iid multivariate-normal sample model. Test Σ=Σ₀, with Σ₀ positive definite and μ unrestricted under both hypotheses. Almost surely the full covariance MLE is M=R/n and −2 log Λ_n=n[tr(Σ₀⁻¹M)−log det(Σ₀⁻¹/²MΣ₀⁻¹/²)−p]. Under the null, with p fixed, this converges in distribution to χ²_{p(p+1)/2}.
Assume AC, p≥1, n≥2 and the iid multivariate-normal sample model. Under Σ=Σ₀ for specified positive-definite Σ₀, tr(Σ₀⁻¹(n−1)S) has exact law χ²_{p(n−1)}, even when n≤p and S is singular.
